question: At T(K), 2 moles of PCl₅(g) are heated in a 10.0 L flask. At equilibrium, 40% of PCl₅ has dissociated into PCl₃ and Cl₂. The Kc for this reaction is
explanation:

question: The number of monochloro derivatives possible for (i) 2-methylpentane, (ii) 3-methylpentane, (iii) n-hexane are x, y, z respectively. The sum x+y+z is
explanation:

3-methylpentane, CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃, has 4 distinct types of hydrogen due to its symmetry (the two equivalent terminal CH₃ groups, the two equivalent CH₂ groups, the branch CH₃, and the central CH), giving y=4 monochloro products

n-Hexane, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃, has 3 distinct types of hydrogen by symmetry (the two equivalent terminal CH₃ groups, the two equivalent CH₂ groups next to them, and the two equivalent middle CH₂ groups), giving z=3 monochloro products

question:

I. Pent-2-ene
II. 2-methylpropene
III. 1-chloropropene
IV. 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene
explanation:
Pent-2-ene (CH₃-CH=CH-CH₂CH₃) has different groups (H,CH₃) on one carbon and (H,C₂H₅) on the other, showing cis-trans isomerism

2-methylpropene has two identical methyl groups on one carbon of the double bond, so no cis-trans isomerism

1-chloropropene (ClCH=CH-CH₃) has different groups (H,Cl) and (H,CH₃) on the two carbons, showing cis-trans isomerism

2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene has two identical methyl groups on each carbon of the double bond, so no cis-trans isomerism

So I and III only exhibit cis-trans isomerism

question: E₁, E₂, E₃ are the emf values of Mg|Mg²⁺(0.1M)||Cu²⁺(1M)|Cu, Mg|Mg²⁺(1M)||Cu²⁺(1M)|Cu, and Mg|Mg²⁺(1M)||Cu²⁺(0.1M)|Cu respectively. The correct order is
explanation:

Cell 1 has the lowest Mg²⁺ concentration, which is favourable, giving the highest emf

Cell 3 has reduced Cu²⁺ concentration, which is unfavourable, giving the lowest emf

So E₁>E₂>E₃

question: The compound used to test for the presence of chloride, bromide, and iodide ions by observing distinct colours in the Layer test (with chlorine water and CCl₄) is based on the fact that
options: Chloride gives an orange colour in CCl₄ layer
Iodide gives a colourless CCl₄ layer
Bromide gives an orange to brown colour in the CCl₄ layer
Chloride, bromide and iodide all give the same colour
explanation:
Chlorine water oxidizes bromide ions to bromine, which dissolves in the CCl₄ layer giving an orange to brown colour

Iodide is oxidized to iodine, which gives a violet/purple colour in CCl₄, not colourless

Chloride is not oxidized by chlorine water since chlorine cannot oxidize itself, so no distinct colour change of this type occurs for chloride

So the identifying feature is that bromide gives an orange to brown colour in the CCl₄ layer

explanation:

question: Among [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺, [Mn(H₂O)₆]²⁺, [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺, [Ni(CO)₄], [Sc(H₂O)₆]³⁺, how many are colourless?
explanation:
A complex is colourless when the metal ion has either an empty (d₀) or a completely filled (d₁₀) set of d-orbitals

[Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺: Cr³⁺ is d₃, coloured
[Mn(H₂O)₆]²⁺: Mn²⁺ is d₅, coloured
[Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺: Co³⁺ is d₆, coloured
[Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺: Cu²⁺ is d₉, coloured
[Ni(CO)₄]: Ni is in the 0 oxidation state here, giving d₁₀, colourless
[Sc(H₂O)₆]³⁺: Sc³⁺ is d₀, colourless

So exactly two of these, [Ni(CO)₄] and [Sc(H₂O)₆]³⁺, are colourless

Count = 2

explanation:

question: Propanoic acid (Y) with Cl₂/red phosphorus gives X (2-chloropropanoic acid). Pentanoic acid (B) with Br₂/red phosphorus then H₂O→A (2-bromopentanoic acid). The pKa relations are
explanation:
The chlorine in X is electron withdrawing, which stabilizes the conjugate base and increases acidity compared to propanoic acid Y

So X is more acidic than Y, meaning pKa(X)<pKa(Y), i.e., Y>X in pKa value

Similarly, the bromine in A withdraws electron density, making A more acidic than B

pKa(A)<pKa(B), i.e., B>A in pKa value

So the relation is Y>X and B>A

question: Among C₆H₅NH₂ (I), C₆H₅NHCH₃ (II), C₆H₅N(CH₃)₂ (III), p-nitroaniline (IV), the correct pair with highest and lowest pKb respectively (in aqueous solution) is
explanation:
p-Nitroaniline (IV) has an electron-withdrawing nitro group para to the amine, which strongly reduces the availability of the nitrogen lone pair through resonance, making it the weakest base and giving it the highest pKb

Among the N-methylated anilines, the methyl groups donate electron density, generally making N-methylaniline (II) a comparatively better electron donor in this set and giving it a lower pKb than aniline itself

So the pair with highest and lowest pKb is IV and II respectively

NH₃ has a lone pair on nitrogen that it readily donates, making it a Lewis base

So BF₃ (Lewis acid) and NH₃ (Lewis base) is the correct pairing
